items.content: The water was cold enough to matter and dark enough to be more than itself — every arm's length became a negotiation, every stroke a small decision to continue. She turned onto her back and looked at the stars and let herself be held by the cold and the dark in equal measure, and thought: this is the only kind of alone that doesn't feel like loss.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the feeling of swimming alone in a lake at night". AI text often produces grammatically perfect sentences with slightly generic emotional beats — look for overly balanced structure and lack of truly surprising word choices.

items.content: The fog had erased all certainty of distance. Buildings arrived suddenly and passed. She knew the street by the sound of her footsteps, by the particular camber of the pavement under her shoes, by the smell of the bakery that meant she was two blocks from home. The city she walked through this morning was not the city she knew — it was the city's idea of itself, temporarily.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "a walk through a city during early morning fog". The polished structure and conceptually inventive metaphors are characteristic of language model output.

items.content: True! —nervous —very, very dreadfully nervous I had been and am; but why will you say that I am mad?
items.explanation: Poe's unreliable narrator defending his sanity, 1843. The breathless dashes and self-interruption create a vocal quality that AI tends to smooth out into more grammatically regular prose.
items.source: Edgar Allan Poe — The Tell-Tale Heart (1843)

items.content: The room darkened by degrees — first the houselights, then the exit signs dimmed, then the absolute black of a space made entirely for watching. She had been to this theatre before but it was always different, this moment — the held breath of an audience becoming a single organism, surrendering its individual silences to a collective one. Then the light on the curtain. Then: begin.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the moment before a concert begins". Notice the even pacing and absence of the kinds of small errors or tonal shifts that appear in prose written under genuine emotional pressure.
